18.t: Working with data: temperature and germination
q: Identify the optimum temperature for each species.
Explain why few bean seeds germinate at 5 °C.
Enzymes such as amylase work slowly, so starch is broken down slowly and respiration releases little energy for growth.
Explain why no bean seeds germinate at 45 °C.
The enzymes are denatured and the embryo cells are damaged or killed.
Suggest how the difference between the species is an adaptation.
Alpine summers are short and cool, so seeds that germinate at low temperatures can grow as soon as the snow melts; their enzymes work best at lower temperatures.
Suggest two control variables and how to keep each constant.
Any two: water (same volume on each paper); light (all in the same dark cupboard); seed size or age (seeds from one batch); number of seeds (50 per dish).
